articles.title: House Oversight Chair looks to ban govt officials' prediction market bets
articles.summary: Chair James Comer released findings from a May investigation covering 1,700 pages of documents and five briefings from prediction market firms, and urges legislation restricting what bets federal employees, lawmakers, and staff can place, up to an outright ban. The probe follows an Army soldier's Polymarket bets on Maduro's capture and a White House teleprompter operator profiting on Kalshi. Kalshi and Polymarket say they have tightened controls, and the Senate passed a resolution in April banning members from such trading.

articles.title: Kava Lend loses about $3.8 million to hack, KAVA token down nearly 40%
articles.summary: An attacker drained about 55.2M KAVA (~$3.76M at pre-attack prices) by exploiting a dormant BUSD market, shrinking its net supply to a tiny nonzero figure so deposit values inflated ~243,000-fold, then borrowing KAVA against it 127 times. About 49.2M KAVA was bridged to BNB Chain through LayerZero and sold for about $2.1M. The attacker had been preparing since November 8. Kava says it is “not an infinite mint” and is contained to Kava Lend, has paused the Axelar bridge, and promises a full incident report. KAVA was down about 39% at publication, and exchanges paused deposits and withdrawals.

articles.title: Tempo Configurable Accounts: PQ + Native Multisig as Default
articles.summary: Tempo's Configurable Accounts (T14) will deploy to mainnet on December 1, introducing post-quantum signature groundwork and native multisig as default account primitives rather than optional add-ons. The upgrade's core claim is friction elimination: both capabilities existed on prior systems, but Configurable Accounts makes them cheap enough to use without weighing cost against benefit. Paradigm frames T14 as a near-completion milestone in "Pragmatic Native Account Abstraction" for the Ethereum ecosystem, with one remaining component, Attestable Accounts, expected in the coming weeks.

articles.title: ChatGPT Wallet Launches for Agentic Commerce
articles.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet, launched Friday, lets OpenAI's always-on agent check out on merchant sites using your own credit card. At checkout, the card network generates a one-time substitute card number capped at the approved amount, so the agent never holds your real card, and you keep your points and dispute rights. Issuers gain visibility versus wallets like Stripe's Link, which charge your card in a second transaction, and merchants may pay lower interchange and see who is buying. Users review and approve each purchase with Face ID, and it is limited to US ChatGPT Pro users 18 or older with Amex, Mastercard, or Visa credit cards only. Under the hood, it uses a vault, enrollment in the networks' agent programs (Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, and Amex ACE), and two sets of headers: Web Bot Auth signatures and user signals in the Forwarded header, with OpenAI working with fraud providers like Forter, Riskified, Sardine, and Signifyd to honor them. Drawbacks are sites still blocking agents, the per-purchase approval, partial card coverage, and slow, token-heavy browser checkout.

articles.title: The Antifragile Internet
articles.summary: October 2026's incident cluster (PHP2Shell exposing 5M+ hosts, Railway decrypting secrets across 100K workspaces, Binance losing $6.3B, and eMudhra issuing a signing key set to "4") frames the argument that AI has collapsed the cost of exploitation to near zero. There are three agent-specific threat vectors: agents as weapons, agents as targets, and agents as impostors. USV's investment thesis closes on crypto: blockchains proved strangers can transact without mutual trust, and the firm expects decentralized reputation, PAP/A2A agent-identity protocols, and permissionless rails to embed in mainstream apps as a two-lane internet takes shape.

articles.title: How We Made $6M+ Exploiting a Single Onchain Edge
articles.summary: A trader and collaborators extracted $6M+ from two Robinhood Chain listings by monitoring two public data sources: Wintermute's on-chain market-making contract whitelists and BitGo's GitHub repository (Robinhood's custody partner). For cashcat, a "hoodeth:cashcat" string in a public BitGo pull request on July 27 and Wintermute's WETH pool approval on August 3 at 17:48 UTC gave days of advance notice. The group accumulated over $1M at around 4% of supply and realized $4M+ when Robinhood listed three days later. A parallel pipeline applied to PONS produced another $2M, with the method requiring no privileged access, only structured monitoring of public contract approval events and custody provider repositories.

articles.title: The current state of crypto markets
articles.summary: There's a scary macro backdrop of cyberattacks and a stock dip. Keeping this in mind, the Binance hack was a major bear signal because stablecoin supply fell more than 5% afterward. The breakout into the 80s was a bull trap. Losing the $74K range low was the real bear signal, and although the $60K mark should hold, a break would ensure capitulation into $40K like in 2022.

articles.title: Nexo report shows government payments dominate its card by value
articles.summary: Alex highlights Nexo's card report: 91% of government payments exceed €1,000, 55% fall between €5,000 and €10,000, and nearly 12% exceed the €10,000 daily limit. He estimates the average government payment at about €6,400 against €80 for the average card transaction, and notes millennials make up about 42% of them. Since Nexo markets borrowing against crypto to avoid capital gains tax, he wonders how many of these were paid in credit mode, effectively tax planning with a card.

articles.title: Arkham Traces $63 Million in Bitget Hack Funds to CoinJoin
articles.summary: Arkham Intelligence traced 847.26 BTC into CoinJoin mixing transactions and identified 959.29 BTC in labeled wallets, accounting for roughly $63 million of the $387.5 million Bitget hack.

articles.title: Initia Confirms Second Exploit in 3 Weeks, $3.27M Stolen
articles.summary: Initia suffered its second security exploit in under three weeks on November 11.

articles.title: Polymarket Weather Arbitrage: $28.7K on $4.2M Volume
articles.summary: A Polymarket wallet buys "No" on weather temperature rungs that forecasts have already eliminated across 44 cities daily, paying 94–99.4 cents per contract to harvest near-certain payouts.

articles.title: Stablecoins lost $16B in 30 days while crypto card volume hit a record
articles.summary: Stablecoin supply fell from $303B on October 15 to under $288B, the steepest 30-day drop since June 2022.
